entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Antigonus of Carystus, a Greek writer on various subjects, flourished in the 3rd century BCE. After some time spent at Athens and travelling, he was summoned to the court of Attalus I (241 BCE–197 BCE) of Pergamum. His chief work is the Successions of Philosophers drawn from personal knowledge, with considerable fragments preserved in Athenaeus and Diogenes Laërtius. His work Ἱστοριῶν παραδόξων συναγωγή, a paradoxographical work chiefly extracted from the Περὶ θαυμασίων ἀκουσμάτων attributed to Aristotle and the Θαυμάσια ("Thaumasia") of Callimachus, survived to modernity.
